items.title: BMO seminorm and the quotient by constants
items.statement:
Complex scalars, Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb R^n$, and the complex $L^p$ and
test-function conventions of [[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]].
A cube is a nondegenerate axis-parallel cube ([[def-multidimensional-rectangle-and-volume]]).
For $b\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^n)$ and a cube $Q$ put
$b_Q:=|Q|^{-1}\int_Qb$, so that $b_Q$ is the mean of $b$ over $Q$, and define
the $\mathrm{BMO}$ seminorm
$\|b\|_{\mathrm{BMO}}:=\sup_Q|Q|^{-1}\int_Q|b-b_Q|\in[0,\infty]$, the supremum
over all cubes, and
$\mathrm{BMO}(\mathbb R^n):=\{b\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}:\|b\|_{\mathrm{BMO}}<\infty\}$.
The mean is optimal up to a factor of $2$ in the average:
$|Q|^{-1}\int_Q|b-b_Q|\le 2\inf_c|Q|^{-1}\int_Q|b-c|\le 2|Q|^{-1}\int_Q|b-b_Q|$
where the infimum is over $c\in\mathbb C$. Moreover $\|b\|_{\mathrm{BMO}}=0$ exactly when $b$ is
constant almost everywhere, so the page works with the quotient
$\mathrm{BMO}(\mathbb R^n)/\mathbb C$ of equivalence classes modulo constants; a
class is written $b\in\mathrm{BMO}/\mathbb C$ and the zero class is the class of
the constants. Replacing cubes by balls in the supremum defines an equivalent
seminorm with comparison constants depending only on $n$.


These assertions follow directly from the averages. For every $c\in\mathbb C$,
$|b_Q-c|\le|Q|^{-1}\int_Q|b-c|$, so the triangle inequality gives the
factor-$2$ upper bound; taking $c=b_Q$ gives the other inequality. For locally integrable functions $b,d$, homogeneity
and $(b+d)_Q=b_Q+d_Q$ give the seminorm laws. If the seminorm is zero,
$b=b_{Q_m}$ almost everywhere on each $Q_m=[-m,m]^n$, $m\ge1$.
The constants agree on their positive-measure overlaps, and the exceptional
set is the union of the explicit measurable null sets
$Q_m\cap\{b\ne b_{Q_1}\}$, hence is null by countable additivity of Lebesgue
measure. Conversely an almost-everywhere constant has zero oscillation.
Thus the quotient also identifies almost-everywhere equal representatives.
Finally, if $E\subseteq F$ are measurable sets of finite positive measure
and $b\in L^1(F)$, then
$|E|^{-1}\int_E|b-b_E|\le2(|F|/|E|)|F|^{-1}\int_F|b-b_F|$.
Every ball is contained in a concentric cube of comparable volume, and every
cube is contained in a concentric ball of comparable volume. Applying this
inequality in both directions proves the cube/ball comparison.

references.title: Mark Williams, Notes on Harmonic Analysis (January 11, 2022)
references.locator: Definition 7.1(b), printed p. 29 (BMO seminorm $\sup_Q|Q|^{-1}\int_Q|f-f_Q|$)

references.title: Juha Kinnunen, Harmonic Analysis (Aalto University lecture notes)
references.locator: Definition 3.1 and the surrounding Moral, printed pp. 34-35

references.title: Terence Tao, Math 247A Lecture Notes 4 (UCLA, Fall 2006)
references.locator: Definition 3.1 and the equivalent $\inf_c$ formulation, printed pp. 11-12

items.strategy: The averaging inequality gives optimality up to factor 2, not exact L1 minimization. Homogeneity and linearity give the seminorm laws. On the explicit nested cubes [-m,m]^n, zero oscillation gives agreeing a.e. constants; the measurable countable null union gives a global a.e. constant. Comparing an enclosing ball and cube in each direction yields equivalent seminorms.

items.title: The Hilbert and Riesz transforms are Calderon-Zygmund operators
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $H$ be the Hilbert transform of
[[cor-hilbert-transform-is-an-ltwo-isometry-and-squares-to-minus-identity|the line]]
and, for $1\le j\le n$, let $R_j$ be the Riesz transform of
[[def-riesz-transforms-on-euclidean-space]]. Then $H$ and each $R_j$ are
Calderon-Zygmund operators with the kernels $k(x)=1/(\pi x)$ and
$K_j(x)=c_nx_j/|x|^{n+1}$: they are $L^2$-bounded with norm at most $1$, and
for every compactly supported $f\in L^2$ and almost every
$x\notin\operatorname{supp}f$ one has $Tf(x)=\int k(x-y)f(y)\,dy$ with the
kernel of $T$. Moreover both kernels are standard $1$-Holder Calderon-Zygmund
kernels with the published constants ($A_2'=2/\pi$ and
$C_n=c_n2^{n+1}(3n+4)$, respectively).

references.title: Mark Williams, Notes on Harmonic Analysis (January 11, 2022)
references.locator: Section 3.1 (Hilbert and Riesz transforms as homogeneous singular integrals) and Definition 3.1 with Remark 3.2(b) ($Tf=W*f$ for Schwartz $f$; $L^2$ extension by density), printed pp. 6-7

references.title: Terence Tao, Math 247A Lecture Notes 4 (UCLA, Fall 2006)
references.locator: the kernel/localisation discussion in Section 3, printed p. 10

items.strategy: Skew-adjointness: for $H$ this is the published skew-adjointness; for $R_j$ it follows from the Plancherel pairing, $\langle R_jf,g\rangle=\int m_j\widehat f\,\overline{\widehat g}=\int\widehat f\,\overline{(-m_j)\widehat g}=\langle f,-R_jg\rangle$, because $m_j$ is purely imaginary. Let $f\in L^2$ be compactly supported and let $\varphi\in C_c^\infty$ be supported off $\operatorname{supp}f$; the Schwartz principal-value formulas identify $T\varphi$ away from $\operatorname{supp}\varphi$ with the ordinary absolutely convergent integral $\int k(y-x)\varphi(x)dx$, so $\langle Tf,\varphi\rangle=-\int f\overline{T\varphi}=\iint k(x-y)f(y)\overline{\varphi(x)}dx\,dy$ by Fubini over the bounded disjoint supports, using oddness of the kernels. Since the pairing against all test functions supported off $\operatorname{supp}f$ determines the $L^2$ class of $Tf$ off that support, the off-support representation holds. The kernel estimates are the published size, first-difference and cancellation bounds, which give standard $1$-Holder status with the stated constants.

items.title: L-infinity embeds continuously into BMO modulo constants
items.statement:
Every $b\in L^\infty(\mathbb R^n)$ lies in $\mathrm{BMO}(\mathbb R^n)$ with
$\|b\|_{\mathrm{BMO}}\le2\|b\|_{L^\infty}$, so the class map
$L^\infty(\mathbb R^n)/\mathbb C\to\mathrm{BMO}(\mathbb R^n)/\mathbb C$ is a
continuous injection. Whether the injection is surjective is not claimed here;
the companion examples page records an unbounded BMO function, which exhibits
strictness independently.

references.title: Mark Williams, Notes on Harmonic Analysis (January 11, 2022)
references.locator: the sentence following Definition 7.1 ($|f|_{\mathrm{BMO}}\le2|f|_{L^\infty}$), printed p. 29

references.title: Juha Kinnunen, Harmonic Analysis (Aalto University lecture notes)
references.locator: Examples 3.5(1), printed p. 37

items.strategy: For every cube, $|Q|^{-1}\int_Q|b-b_Q|\le|Q|^{-1}\int_Q(|b|+|b_Q|)\le2\|b\|_{L^\infty}$. Injectivity follows from the zero-seminorm characterisation in the definition item: a bounded function of zero mean oscillation is almost everywhere constant. The strictness witness is deliberately not consumed here, because this corollary may not depend on a companion B-page item; the witness is established on the companion page on its own.

items.title: BMO averages on nested cubes grow at most logarithmically
items.statement:
There is $C_n<\infty$ such that for every $b\in\mathrm{BMO}(\mathbb R^n)$ and
all cubes $Q\subseteq R$, writing $\ell(Q)$ for the side length,
$|b_Q-b_R|\le C_n\bigl(1+\log_2(\ell(R)/\ell(Q))\bigr)\|b\|_{\mathrm{BMO}}$.

references.title: Mark Williams, Notes on Harmonic Analysis (January 11, 2022)
references.locator: Lemma 7.4 (nested cubes with side lengths halving: $|f_{Q_n}-f_{Q_0}|\le2dn|f|_{\mathrm{BMO}}$), printed p. 30

references.title: Juha Kinnunen, Harmonic Analysis (Aalto University lecture notes)
references.locator: the telescoping consequence of Lemma 3.2 before Theorem 3.15, printed pp. 44-45

references.title: Terence Tao, Math 247A Lecture Notes 4 (UCLA, Fall 2006)
references.locator: the Calderon-Zygmund iteration section, printed p. 13

items.strategy: Choose m minimal with 2^m ell(Q)>=2ell(R), so the concentric dyadic enlargement contains R and has volume <4^n|R|. Telescoping mean differences gives m2^n BMO; comparison with R adds 4^n BMO, and m<2+log2(ell(R)/ell(Q)) gives the claimed constant. Q=R is treated separately.

items.title: BMO functions pair uniformly with H1 atoms
items.statement:
Let $b\in\mathrm{BMO}(\mathbb R^n)$ and let $a$ be an $H^1$ atom supported in a
cube $Q$, i.e. a $(1,\infty,0)$-atom in the sense of
[[def-hp-atom-with-moment-order]]: $a$ vanishes off $Q$, $|a|\le|Q|^{-1}$
almost everywhere and $\int a=0$. Then the integral $\int ab$ converges
absolutely and $\bigl|\int ab\bigr|\le\|b\|_{\mathrm{BMO}}$, with the bound
independent of the atom and of $Q$.

references.title: Mark Williams, Notes on Harmonic Analysis (January 11, 2022)
references.locator: the first part of Definition 7.39 (the pairing $L_b(g)=\int bg$ and its bound), printed p. 47

items.strategy: Since $\int a=0$, subtract the mean of $b$ over the cube: $\int ab=\int a(b-b_Q)$. Then $\bigl|\int a(b-b_Q)\bigr|\le\|a\|_{L^\infty}\int_Q|b-b_Q|\le |Q|^{-1}\cdot|Q|\cdot\|b\|_{\mathrm{BMO}}=\|b\|_{\mathrm{BMO}}$. Absolute convergence holds because $a$ is bounded with compact support and $b$ is locally integrable. No cancellation beyond the zero-th moment is used at $p=1$.

items.title: John-Nirenberg stopping cubes have geometric decay
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $b\in\mathrm{BMO}(\mathbb R^n)$, let $Q$ be an
all-generations dyadic cube and let $s>\|b\|_{\mathrm{BMO}}$. Then there are
families of dyadic subcubes $Q^{(k)}_j\subseteq Q$, $k\ge1$, pairwise
disjoint for each fixed $k$, such that, with $Q^{(0)}_1:=Q$:
(i) each $Q^{(k)}_j$ is contained in a unique level-$(k-1)$ stopping cube.
Its immediate dyadic parent is contained in that stopping cube but need not
belong to the preceding stopping family; (ii) for every $k$,
$\sum_j|Q^{(k)}_j|\le(\|b\|_{\mathrm{BMO}}/s)^k|Q|$; and (iii) for every
$k\ge1$, $|b-b_Q|\le k2^ns$ almost everywhere on
$Q\setminus\bigcup_jQ^{(k)}_j$, and a fortiori $|b-b_Q|\le2^{nk}s$ there, so
$\{x\in Q:|b-b_Q|>2^{nk}s\}\subseteq\bigcup_jQ^{(k)}_j$ up to a Lebesgue-null
set.

references.title: Juha Kinnunen, Harmonic Analysis (Aalto University lecture notes)
references.locator: Theorem 3.15 and its proof (recursive Calderon-Zygmund decomposition, bounded overlap and the $2^{nk}$ level bound), printed pp. 44-48

references.title: Mark Williams, Notes on Harmonic Analysis (January 11, 2022)
references.locator: Theorem 7.5, proof steps 1-4 ((A-k)-(E-k) and (7.8)), printed pp. 29-31

references.title: Brooke Wilson, Math 581A Classical and Multilinear Harmonic Analysis (University of Washington, Fall 2024), lecture 18
references.locator: the dyadic John-Nirenberg induction, scanned pages 1-3

items.strategy: Use maximal dyadic stopping at fixed s>BMO on each current stopping cube. The families are disjoint at each fixed stopping level; their immediate dyadic parents need not be stopping parents. Iterated volume ratio BMO/s gives geometric decay. Mean jumps <=2^n s and the exit bound <=s give k2^n s off level k. Countable Choice is inherited from maximal/decomposition, differentiation and countable-union suppliers.

items.title: Range truncations preserve the BMO seminorm up to a constant
items.statement:
For every real-valued $b\in\mathrm{BMO}(\mathbb R^n)$ and every $c\in\mathbb R$
the one-sided truncations satisfy
$\|\max(b,c)\|_{\mathrm{BMO}}\le\tfrac32\|b\|_{\mathrm{BMO}}$ and
$\|\min(b,c)\|_{\mathrm{BMO}}\le\tfrac32\|b\|_{\mathrm{BMO}}$; consequently for
$-\infty<L\le K<\infty$ the two-sided truncation
$b_{[L,K]}:=\min\bigl(K,\max(L,b)\bigr)$ satisfies
$\|b_{[L,K]}\|_{\mathrm{BMO}}\le\tfrac94\|b\|_{\mathrm{BMO}}$. For a
complex-valued $b$ the componentwise truncation
$b_M:=\min(M,\max(-M,\operatorname{Re}b))+i\min(M,\max(-M,\operatorname{Im}b))$
satisfies $|b_M|\le|b|$, $b_M\to b$ pointwise as $M\to\infty$, and
$\|b_M\|_{\mathrm{BMO}}\le\tfrac92\|b\|_{\mathrm{BMO}}$.

references.title: Juha Kinnunen, Harmonic Analysis (Aalto University lecture notes)
references.locator: Theorem 3.6(1) and Remark 3.7 (truncation $f_k=\min\{\max\{f,-k\},k\}$ with $\|f_k\|_*\lesssim\tfrac94\|f\|_*$), printed pp. 40-41

references.title: Mark Williams, Notes on Harmonic Analysis (January 11, 2022)
references.locator: Definition 7.39(3) and footnote 61 (the truncation $f^{KL}=...$ and its contract), printed pp. 46-47

items.strategy: Write $\max(b,c)=c+(b-c)^+$ and $(b-c)^+=\tfrac12\bigl((b-c)+|b-c|\bigr)$, so it suffices to bound the mean oscillation of $|b-c|$. For every cube $Q$ and every constant $d$ one has $|Q|^{-1}\int_Q\bigl||b-c|-(|b-c|)_Q\bigr|\le2|Q|^{-1}\int_Q||b-c|-d|$ (the mean is within the average deviation), and choosing $d=|b_Q-c|$ gives $||b-c|-d|\le|b-b_Q|$, hence the oscillation of $|b-c|$ is at most $2\|b\|_{\mathrm{BMO}}$; the triangle inequality for the seminorm finishes the one-sided bound, and applying it twice gives the two-sided one. The complex statement follows from $\|\operatorname{Re}b\|_{\mathrm{BMO}}\le\|b\|_{\mathrm{BMO}}$ for each part; the pointwise and domination statements are immediate from the componentwise definition.

items.title: Calderon-Zygmund operators map L-infinity to BMO
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $T$ be a Calderon-Zygmund operator with kernel $k$
in the sense of [[def-calderon-zygmund-kernel-and-principal-value-operator]]: $k$
satisfies the annular size bound with constant $A_1$ and Hormander's condition
with constant $A_2$, $T$ is $L^2$-bounded with norm $B$ and satisfies the
off-support representation (3) of that definition. Assume moreover that $k$ is
standard $\delta$-Holder with constant $A_2'$ for some $0<\delta\le1$
([[def-standard-holder-calderon-zygmund-kernel]]). Fix
$\lambda_n:=1+4\sqrt n$, chosen so that
$|a-y|\ge2\sqrt n\,\ell(Q)\ge2|x-a|$ whenever $x,a\in Q$ and
$y\notin\lambda_nQ$. For a cube $Q$ and a point $a\in Q$ put, for $x\in Q$,
$(Tb)_Q(x):=T(b\mathbf 1_{\lambda_nQ})(x)+\int_{\mathbb R^n\setminus\lambda_nQ}\bigl[k(x-y)-k(a-y)\bigr]b(y)\,dy$,
where $\lambda_nQ$ is the concentric cube with side length $\lambda_n\ell(Q)$
and $b\in L^\infty(\mathbb R^n)$. Then: (i) the tail integral converges
absolutely for every $x\in Q$; (ii) for nested cubes $Q\subseteq R$ the
difference $(Tb)_Q-(Tb)_R$ is almost everywhere constant on $Q$, so the
localisations define a class $Tb\in\mathrm{BMO}(\mathbb R^n)/\mathbb C$; (iii)
$\|Tb\|_{\mathrm{BMO}}\le C_{n,\delta}(A_2'+B)\|b\|_{L^\infty}$; and (iv) if in
addition $b\in L^2(\mathbb R^n)$, then the class $Tb$ is the class of the $L^2$
function $Tb$ defined by the operator, modulo constants.

references.title: Mark Williams, Notes on Harmonic Analysis (January 11, 2022)
references.locator: Proposition 7.7 and (7.11) (the local/far decomposition with the kernel difference and the $L^2$ bound), printed p. 32

references.title: Terence Tao, Math 247A Lecture Notes 4 (UCLA, Fall 2006)
references.locator: Proposition 3.4 and its proof (the localisation $Tf=T(f\mathbf 1_{2B})+T(f\mathbf 1_{\mathbb R^d\setminus2B})$ with the constant $c_B$), printed p. 12

items.strategy: Absolute convergence in (i): for $x,a\in Q$ and $y\notin\lambda_nQ$ one has $|x-a|\le\sqrt n\,\ell(Q)$ and $|a-y|\ge2\sqrt n\,\ell(Q)\ge2|x-a|$, so the standard $\delta$-Holder bound makes the tail integrand bounded by $A_2'n^{\delta/2}\ell(Q)^\delta|a-y|^{-n-\delta}\|b\|_{L^\infty}$, which is integrable over the complement. For (iii), take the constant $c=0$ (the mean-deviation bound allows any constant) and bound the two terms: the local term is controlled by Cauchy-Schwarz and the $L^2$ bound, $|Q|^{-1}\int_Q|T(b\mathbf 1_{\lambda_nQ})|\le|Q|^{-1/2}B\|b\|_{L^\infty}|\lambda_nQ|^{1/2}\le \lambda_n^{n/2}B\|b\|_{L^\infty}$, and the tail term by the same Holder bound integrated over the complement, $|Q|^{-1}\int_Q\int_{\mathbb R^n\setminus\lambda_nQ}|k(x-y)-k(a-y)||b(y)|\,dy\,dx\le A_2'n^{\delta/2}\ell(Q)^\delta\|b\|_{L^\infty}\int_{|z|\ge2\sqrt n\ell(Q)}|z|^{-n-\delta}\,dz\le C_n\delta^{-1}A_2'\|b\|_{L^\infty}$, so the mean oscillation of $(Tb)_Q$ is at most $C_n(\lambda_n^{n/2}B+\delta^{-1}A_2')\|b\|_{L^\infty}$. For (ii), compute $(Tb)_R-(Tb)_Q$ on $Q$: since $b\mathbf 1_{\lambda_nR\setminus\lambda_nQ}$ is a compactly supported $L^2$ function and $T$ satisfies the off-support representation, $T(b\mathbf 1_{\lambda_nR})(x)=T(b\mathbf 1_{\lambda_nQ})(x)+\int_{\lambda_nR\setminus\lambda_nQ}k(x-y)b(y)\,dy$ for almost every $x\in Q$; the difference is then the sum of the absolutely convergent expressions $\int_{\lambda_nR\setminus\lambda_nQ}k(a_Q-y)b(y)dy$ and $\int_{(\lambda_nR)^c}\bigl[k(a_Q-y)-k(a_R-y)\bigr]b(y)dy$, both independent of $x$, the second bounded by Hormander's condition with $v=a_R-a_Q$. For (iv), approximate $b$ by $b_R=b\mathbf 1_{B(0,R)}$ in $L^2$: then $Tb_R\to Tb$ in $L^2$, hence almost everywhere on $Q$ along a subsequence; for two points $x,x'$ of that full-measure convergence set the off-support representation on $Q$ gives $Tb_R(x)-Tb_R(x')=T(b\mathbf 1_{\lambda_nQ})(x)-T(b\mathbf 1_{\lambda_nQ})(x')+\int_{B(0,R)\setminus\lambda_nQ}\bigl[k(x-y)-k(x'-y)\bigr]b(y)\,dy$; since $|x'-y|\ge2\sqrt n\,\ell(Q)\ge2|x-x'|$ on $(\lambda_nQ)^c$, the pointwise Holder bound makes the last integral converge as $R\to\infty$ to $\int_{\mathbb R^n\setminus\lambda_nQ}[k(x-y)-k(x'-y)]b(y)\,dy$, while the same computation applied to $(Tb)_Q$ gives the same expression for $(Tb)_Q(x)-(Tb)_Q(x')$; hence $Tb(x)-Tb(x')=(Tb)_Q(x)-(Tb)_Q(x')$ for almost every pair, so $Tb-(Tb)_Q$ is almost everywhere constant on $Q$.

items.title: The Hilbert and Riesz transforms map L-infinity to BMO
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. The Hilbert transform $H$ on $\mathbb R$ and the Riesz
transforms $R_1,\dots,R_n$ on $\mathbb R^n$ extend to bounded maps
 $L^\infty(\mathbb R^d)\to\mathrm{BMO}(\mathbb R^d)/\mathbb C$,
where $d=1$ for $T=H$ and $d=n$ for $T=R_j$: for every
$b\in L^\infty(\mathbb R^d)$ the
class of $Tb$ is well defined modulo constants, agrees with the $L^2$ action of
$T$ when $b\in L^2$, and satisfies $\|Tb\|_{\mathrm{BMO}}\le C_d\|b\|_{L^\infty}$
with a dimensional constant.

references.title: Mark Williams, Notes on Harmonic Analysis (January 11, 2022)
references.locator: Proposition 7.7 (SIO mapping property), printed p. 32

references.title: Terence Tao, Math 247A Lecture Notes 4 (UCLA, Fall 2006)
references.locator: Proposition 3.4, printed p. 12

items.strategy: The preceding lemma verifies the Calderon-Zygmund operator contract of the mapping theorem: the kernels are standard $1$-Holder with the published constants and the operators satisfy the off-support representation with $L^2$ norm at most $1$. Applying the mapping theorem gives the bound and the agreement with the $L^2$ action.

items.title: John-Nirenberg exponential inequality
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. There are constants $c_n,C_n\in(0,\infty)$ such that
for every $b\in\mathrm{BMO}(\mathbb R^n)$, every cube $Q$ and every
$\lambda>0$,
$\bigl|\{x\in Q:|b(x)-b_Q|>\lambda\}\bigr|\le C_n|Q|\exp\bigl(-c_n\lambda/\|b\|_{\mathrm{BMO}}\bigr)$.
If $\|b\|_{\mathrm{BMO}}=0$ then $b$ is constant almost everywhere and the
left-hand side is $0$ for every $\lambda>0$, which is the interpretation used
throughout.

references.title: Juha Kinnunen, Harmonic Analysis (Aalto University lecture notes)
references.locator: Theorem 3.15, printed p. 44

references.title: Mark Williams, Notes on Harmonic Analysis (January 11, 2022)
references.locator: Theorem 7.5 (take $b=e$ in (7.8)), printed pp. 29-31

references.title: Terence Tao, Math 247A Lecture Notes 4 (UCLA, Fall 2006)
references.locator: Proposition 3.5 for balls, printed pp. 12-13

references.title: Brooke Wilson, Math 581A Classical and Multilinear Harmonic Analysis (University of Washington, Fall 2024), lecture 18
references.locator: the dyadic John-Nirenberg inequality, scanned page 2

items.strategy: Cover an arbitrary cube by at most 2^n cubes of one fixed dyadic generation, with comparable volume, rather than a single dyadic ancestor. Compare each mean through a common enclosing cube. Use the linear level bound k2^n s with s=2^(n+1)BMO and k=floor((lambda-B_n BMO)/(2^n s)); the geometric stopping measure then gives an exponential in lambda/BMO. Trivial measure bounds cover small levels, and zero seminorm is handled separately. Countable Choice is inherited from the stopping supplier.

items.title: BMO oscillation norms in Lq are equivalent
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]).

Let $1\le q<\infty$ and for $b\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^n)$ put
$\|b\|_{\mathrm{BMO},q}:=\sup_Q\bigl(|Q|^{-1}\int_Q|b-b_Q|^q\bigr)^{1/q}\in[0,\infty]$,
the supremum over all cubes. Then there are constants
$0<c_{n,q}\le C_{n,q}<\infty$ such that
$c_{n,q}\|b\|_{\mathrm{BMO}}\le\|b\|_{\mathrm{BMO},q}\le C_{n,q}\|b\|_{\mathrm{BMO}}$
for every $b\in\mathrm{BMO}(\mathbb R^n)$; indeed
$\bigl(|Q|^{-1}\int_Q|b-b_Q|^q\bigr)^{1/q}\le C_{n,q}\|b\|_{\mathrm{BMO}}$ for
every cube $Q$. In particular every $\mathrm{BMO}$ function lies in
$L^q_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^n)$.

references.title: Mark Williams, Notes on Harmonic Analysis (January 11, 2022)
references.locator: Proposition 7.6 and (7.10), printed p. 32

references.title: Juha Kinnunen, Harmonic Analysis (Aalto University lecture notes)
references.locator: Theorem 3.28 (equivalence of $\|\cdot\|_{*,p}$ and $\|\cdot\|_*$), printed pp. 53-54

references.title: Terence Tao, Math 247A Lecture Notes 4 (UCLA, Fall 2006)
references.locator: Corollary 3.6, printed p. 13

items.strategy: Assume Countable Choice inherited from John-Nirenberg. The q=1 lower bound is equality; for q>1 use Holder when its RHS is finite and treat infinite RHS as trivial. Layer cake and the exponential tail yield a finite gamma-type integral and the upper bound; zero seminorm gives zero oscillation. Finite cube coverings and adding the finite local mean yield local Lq integrability.

items.title: L2-normalised H1 atoms have uniformly bounded H1 norm
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Fix an admissible kernel $\varphi$ with
$\int\varphi\ne0$ and an auxiliary integer order
$\widetilde N\ge\max\{N_0(n,1,\varphi),n+1\}$ for the grand-maximal
characterisation. Let $a$ be a $(1,2)$-atom supported in a cube $Q$: $a$
vanishes off $Q$, $\int a=0$ and
$\bigl(|Q|^{-1}\int_Q|a|^2\bigr)^{1/2}\le|Q|^{-1}$. Then
$\|a\|_{H^1}=\|M^0_\varphi a\|_{L^1}\le C_{n,\widetilde N,\varphi}$, with the
constant independent of $Q$ and the atom.

references.title: Mark Williams, Notes on Harmonic Analysis (January 11, 2022)
references.locator: Definition 7.34 and Proposition 7.35 (every $L^2$ atom has $|A|_{H^1}\lesssim_n1$), printed pp. 40-41

items.strategy: Sum the full near-ball and annular convolution estimates to bound the grand maximal function by C(n,Ntilde)M(|a|). L2 maximal boundedness and a comparable enlarged-cube volume control the near integral. Mean-zero subtraction and derivative decay for t<=r/2 or t>r/2 give ell(Q)r^(-n-1), with summable dyadic shells. Only after proving the finite grand L1 norm use the independently valid radial<=grand comparison. Constants depend on the fixed n,Ntilde,phi, never the atom or cube.

items.title: Mean-zero L2 functions on a cube embed continuously into H1
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice, and fix the admissible kernel $\varphi$ and auxiliary
order $\widetilde N$ of [[lem-ltwo-atoms-have-uniform-hone-quasinorm]]. There is
$C_{n,\widetilde N,\varphi}<\infty$ such that for every cube $Q$ and
every $f\in L^2(\mathbb R^n)$ with $\operatorname{supp}f\subseteq Q$ and
$\int_Qf=0$, the class of $f$ lies in $H^1(\mathbb R^n)$ and
$\|f\|_{H^1}\le C_{n,\widetilde N,\varphi}|Q|^{1/2}\|f\|_{L^2}$.

references.title: Mark Williams, Notes on Harmonic Analysis (January 11, 2022)
references.locator: the inequality $\|g\|_{H^1}\le c|B|^{1/2}\|g\|_{L^2}$ used in the proof of Theorem 7.40(b), printed p. 47

items.strategy: If $f=0$ the claim is trivial; otherwise put $a:=f/(|Q|^{1/2}\|f\|_{L^2})$. Then $a$ vanishes off $Q$, $\int a=0$ and $(|Q|^{-1}\int_Q|a|^2)^{1/2}=|Q|^{-1}$, so it is a $(1,2)$-atom. The preceding atom lemma gives $\|a\|_{H^1}\le C_{n,\widetilde N,\varphi}$. Homogeneity yields $\|f\|_{H^1}=|Q|^{1/2}\|f\|_{L^2}\|a\|_{H^1}\le C_{n,\widetilde N,\varphi}|Q|^{1/2}\|f\|_{L^2}$.

items.title: Finite atomic sums are dense in H1
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. The finite linear combinations of $H^1$ atoms are
dense in $H^1(\mathbb R^n)$: for every $f\in H^1(\mathbb R^n)$ and every
$\varepsilon>0$ there are finitely many atoms $a_1,\dots,a_N$ and coefficients
$\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_N$ with
$\bigl\|f-\sum_{1\le j\le N}\lambda_ja_j\bigr\|_{H^1}<\varepsilon$.

references.title: Mark Williams, Notes on Harmonic Analysis (January 11, 2022)
references.locator: Proposition 7.36 and the density statement in Definition 7.39(1) ('$H^1_0\subset H^1$ is the dense subset of finite linear combinations of atoms'), printed pp. 41 and 47

items.strategy: The atomic characterisation gives $f=\sum_j\lambda_ja_j$ with $(\lambda_j)\in\ell^1$ and convergence in the $H^1$ quasi-norm; the partial sums are finite atomic combinations and converge to $f$, which is the assertion.

items.title: Bounded H1 functionals have compatible local L2 representatives
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and fix the kernel $\varphi$ and auxiliary order
$\widetilde N$ of [[lem-mean-zero-ltwo-functions-on-a-cube-embed-continuously-in-hone]].
Let $\Lambda\in(H^1(\mathbb R^n))^*$ and let
$L^2_0(Q)$ be the closed subspace of $L^2(\mathbb R^n)$ of functions supported
in the cube $Q$ with $\int_Qf=0$ (equivalently, mean $0$ when $|Q|>0$).
For every cube $Q$ there is a unique
$u_Q\in L^2_0(Q)$ with $\Lambda(f)=\int_Qu_Qf$ for every $f\in L^2_0(Q)$;
moreover $Q\subseteq R$ implies that $u_Q-u_R$ is almost everywhere constant
on $Q$. Consequently there are a locally integrable function $u$ on
$\mathbb R^n$, unique up to additive constants, and for every cube $Q$ a
constant $c_Q$ with $u-u_Q=c_Q$ almost everywhere on $Q$.

references.title: Mark Williams, Notes on Harmonic Analysis (January 11, 2022)
references.locator: Theorem 7.40(b), construction of $F^Q$ and the subsequent gluing, printed pp. 47-48

references.title: Brooke Wilson, Math 581A Classical and Multilinear Harmonic Analysis (University of Washington, Fall 2024), lecture 20
references.locator: the reverse inclusion and its Riesz-representation step, scanned pages 1-3

items.strategy: The support subspace is closed and its mean functional continuous by Cauchy-Schwarz. Restrict Lambda using the fixed-kernel mean-zero embedding, apply first-variable-linear Riesz and conjugate its vector to obtain the bilinear u_Q. For nested cubes, test h=u_Q-u_R with conjugate(h-mean_Q(h))*1_Q to prove constancy. Select countably many measurable representatives, adjust constants on nested cubes, remove the null union and assign zero there; this gives the global representative and uniqueness modulo constants. Null cubes have L2_0(Q)={0}; nested compatibility on them is vacuous, and mean tests are used only when |Q|>0.

items.title: Bounded BMO functions dualise H1 boundedly
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice, fix the $H^1$ kernel $\varphi$ and admissible atomic
order $\widetilde N$ used in [[thm-atomic-characterisation-of-real-hp]]. There
is $C_{n,\widetilde N,\varphi}<\infty$ such that for every
$b\in L^\infty(\mathbb R^n)\cap\mathrm{BMO}(\mathbb R^n)$ and every
$f\in H^1(\mathbb R^n)$ the integral $\int fb$ converges absolutely and
$\bigl|\int fb\bigr|\le C_{n,\widetilde N,\varphi}\|b\|_{\mathrm{BMO}}\|f\|_{H^1}$.

references.title: Mark Williams, Notes on Harmonic Analysis (January 11, 2022)
references.locator: (7.69) and the sentence following it (write $L_bf$ using the atomic decomposition, use Cauchy-Schwarz and the properties of atoms), printed p. 47

items.strategy: Use the atomic characterisation of $H^1$ for the fixed kernel $\varphi$ and order $\widetilde N$: $f=\sum_j\lambda_ja_j$ in $\mathcal S'$ and in the $H^1$ norm, with $(\lambda_j)\in\ell^1$ and $\sum_j|\lambda_j|\le C_{n,\widetilde N,\varphi}\|f\|_{H^1}$. The partial sums obey $\|\sum_{j\le N}\lambda_ja_j\|_{L^1}\le\sum_{j\le N}|\lambda_j|$, so the series also converges absolutely in $L^1$ to $f$; since $b$ is bounded, $\int fb=\sum_j\lambda_j\int a_jb$, absolutely. Each atom pairing is bounded by $\|b\|_{\mathrm{BMO}}$, hence $|\int fb|\le C_{n,\widetilde N,\varphi}\|b\|_{\mathrm{BMO}}\|f\|_{H^1}$.

items.title: The dual representative has uniformly bounded BMO oscillation
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice, fix the $H^1$ kernel $\varphi$ and auxiliary order
$\widetilde N$ of [[lem-mean-zero-ltwo-functions-on-a-cube-embed-continuously-in-hone]],
let $\Lambda\in(H^1(\mathbb R^n))^*$ and let $u$ be the representative of the
preceding lemma. Then $u\in\mathrm{BMO}(\mathbb R^n)$ and
$\|u\|_{\mathrm{BMO}}\le C_{n,\widetilde N,\varphi}\|\Lambda\|$, with the
constant independent of $\Lambda$.

references.title: Mark Williams, Notes on Harmonic Analysis (January 11, 2022)
references.locator: the closing computation of Theorem 7.40 ('show $\sup_Q|Q|^{-1}\int_Q|b-b_Q|\lesssim_n|L|_{H^1\to\mathbb C}$') and (7.72)-(7.74), printed pp. 47-48

references.title: Brooke Wilson, Math 581A Classical and Multilinear Harmonic Analysis (University of Washington, Fall 2024), lecture 20
references.locator: the norm bound for the representing function, scanned pages 2-3

items.strategy: Fix a nondegenerate cube $Q$. Since $u-u_Q$ is constant on $Q$ and $u_Q$ has mean zero, the mean oscillation of $u$ on $Q$ is $|Q|^{-1}\int_Q|u_Q|\le|Q|^{-1/2}\|u_Q\|_{L^2(Q)}$. The mean-zero embedding bounds the restricted functional by $C_{n,\widetilde N,\varphi}|Q|^{1/2}\|\Lambda\|$; Riesz isometry gives the same bound for $\|u_Q\|_{L^2(Q)}$. Thus every nondegenerate cube oscillation is at most $C_{n,\widetilde N,\varphi}\|\Lambda\|$, which gives the BMO bound.

items.title: BMO classes define bounded functionals on H1
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice, with the fixed $H^1$ kernel $\varphi$ and
admissible atomic order $\widetilde N$ of [[thm-atomic-characterisation-of-real-hp]].
For every $b\in\mathrm{BMO}(\mathbb R^n)$ there is a
unique bounded linear functional $\Lambda_b\in(H^1(\mathbb R^n))^*$ with
$\Lambda_b(a)=\int ab$ for every $H^1$ atom $a$, and
$\|\Lambda_b\|\le C_{n,\widetilde N,\varphi}\|b\|_{\mathrm{BMO}}$ with the
constant independent of $b$. The
map $b\mapsto\Lambda_b$ is linear, annihilates constants, and therefore factors
through $\mathrm{BMO}(\mathbb R^n)/\mathbb C$; on every finite sum of atoms $g$
one has $\Lambda_b(g)=\int gb$.

references.title: Mark Williams, Notes on Harmonic Analysis (January 11, 2022)
references.locator: Definition 7.39 (the action of $b\in\mathrm{BMO}$ on $H^1$, including the truncation and Banach-Alaoglu step) and (7.69), printed p. 47

items.strategy: (1) Bounded case. For $b\in L^\infty\cap\mathrm{BMO}$ define $\Lambda$ on finite atomic sums by $g\mapsto\int gb$; this is well defined because finite sums equal as $H^1$ elements agree almost everywhere as $L^1$ functions. The preceding lemma gives $|\Lambda(g)|\le C_{n,\widetilde N,\varphi}\|b\|_{\mathrm{BMO}}\|g\|_{H^1}$, so $\Lambda$ extends uniquely to a bounded functional by density. (2) For general $b$, use the componentwise truncations $b_M$: their BMO seminorm is at most $\tfrac92\|b\|_{\mathrm{BMO}}$, so the resulting functionals lie in the dual ball of radius $\tfrac92C_{n,\widetilde N,\varphi}\|b\|_{\mathrm{BMO}}$. Banach--Alaoglu under AC gives a weak-star cluster point, and dominated convergence on each atom identifies its values as $\int ab$. Uniqueness follows from atom density; linearity, vanishing on constants and the finite-sum identity follow from those atom values.

items.title: BMO classes are determined by their pairings with H1 atoms
items.statement:
Let $b\in\mathrm{BMO}(\mathbb R^n)$ and suppose $\int ab=0$ for every $H^1$
atom $a$. Then $b$ is constant almost everywhere. Equivalently, the evaluation
map on atoms is injective on $\mathrm{BMO}/\mathbb C$.

references.title: Mark Williams, Notes on Harmonic Analysis (January 11, 2022)
references.locator: Theorem 7.40(a) (injectivity: test against $g=b-b_Q$), printed p. 47

references.title: Brooke Wilson, Math 581A Classical and Multilinear Harmonic Analysis (University of Washington, Fall 2024), lecture 20
references.locator: the injectivity of the pairing, scanned page 1

items.strategy: Use the explicit measurable phase h=conjugate(b-b_Q)/|b-b_Q| on its nonzero set, zero elsewhere. The bounded mean-zero test g=(h-h_Q)1_Q is an atom multiple, or zero; atom annihilation gives integral_Q |b-b_Q|=0. The BMO zero-kernel property yields a.e. constancy. Apply this to differences to get injectivity, with no local L2 or choice prerequisite.

items.title: Real H1-BMO duality
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice, with the fixed $H^1$ kernel $\varphi$ and auxiliary
order $\widetilde N$ used in
[[lem-mean-zero-ltwo-functions-on-a-cube-embed-continuously-in-hone]]. The map
$\Phi:\mathrm{BMO}(\mathbb R^n)/\mathbb C\to(H^1(\mathbb R^n))^*$,
$b\mapsto\Lambda_b$ of the preceding theorem is a linear bijection, and there
are constants $0<c_{n,\widetilde N,\varphi}\le
C_{n,\widetilde N,\varphi}<\infty$ with
$c_{n,\widetilde N,\varphi}\|b\|_{\mathrm{BMO}}\le\|\Lambda_b\|\le
C_{n,\widetilde N,\varphi}\|b\|_{\mathrm{BMO}}$ for every class $b$. Thus
$(H^1(\mathbb R^n))^*$ is isomorphic to
$\mathrm{BMO}(\mathbb R^n)/\mathbb C$ with equivalent norms.

references.title: Mark Williams, Notes on Harmonic Analysis (January 11, 2022)
references.locator: Theorem 7.40 ((a) and (b)) and the surrounding construction, printed pp. 47-48

references.title: Brooke Wilson, Math 581A Classical and Multilinear Harmonic Analysis (University of Washington, Fall 2024), lecture 21
references.locator: the dyadic atomic decomposition and duality template, scanned pages 1-3

references.title: Brooke Wilson, Math 581A Classical and Multilinear Harmonic Analysis (University of Washington, Fall 2024), lecture 22
references.locator: the concluding duality step, scanned pages 1-2

items.strategy: (i) $\Phi$ is well defined and bounded by the preceding theorem, injective by the atom-pairing lemma, and factors through constants. The norm constants may depend on the fixed kernel $\varphi$ and the auxiliary order $\widetilde N$. (ii) Given $\Lambda\in(H^1)^*$, the two preceding lemmas produce $u\in\mathrm{BMO}$ with $\|u\|_{\mathrm{BMO}}\le C_{n,\widetilde N,\varphi}\|\Lambda\|$ and local Riesz representatives $u_Q$ with $u-u_Q$ constant on every cube. For an H1 atom $a$ supported in $Q$, $a\in L^2_0(Q)$, so $\Lambda(a)=\int_Qau_Q=\int_Qau=\Lambda_u(a)$; the constant disappears because $\int a=0$. Density of finite atomic sums extends this equality to H1, proving surjectivity. (iii) Applying (ii) to $\Lambda_b$ and using injectivity shows that the resulting BMO representative differs from $b$ by a constant, giving the reverse norm inequality with the same parameter-dependent constants.

title: BMO, John-Nirenberg, and H1 Duality — Examples

items.title: The BMO seminorm is unchanged by adding a constant
items.statement:
For $b\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^n)$ and $c\in\mathbb C$ one has
$(b+c)_Q=b_Q+c$ for every cube $Q$ and hence
$\|b+c\|_{\mathrm{BMO}}=\|b\|_{\mathrm{BMO}}$; so the BMO seminorm descends to
the quotient $\mathrm{BMO}/\mathbb C$ and is a norm there.

references.title: Juha Kinnunen, Harmonic Analysis (Aalto University lecture notes)
references.locator: Definition 3.1 and the sentence 'The BMO norm is the smallest constant M...', printed p. 35

items.strategy: Linearity of the integral gives $(b+c)_Q=b_Q+c$, so $|(b+c)-(b+c)_Q|=|b-b_Q|$; taking the supremum gives the identity, and the quotient statement is immediate from the zero-seminorm characterisation in the definition.

items.title: Recorded: one dyadic grid is not enough for BMO
items.statement:
Recorded result (Mei 2003), not proved here. On the circle
$\mathbb T=\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z$, let $\mathrm{BMO}_D(\mathbb T)$ be the
dyadic BMO space of one fixed dyadic grid and let
$\varphi\mapsto\varphi(\cdot-2\delta\pi)$ be a translate by a shift $0<\delta<1$ satisfying
$d(\delta):=\inf_{m\ge0,\,k\in\mathbb Z}2^m|\delta-k2^{-m}|>0$
(for example $\delta=1/3$). Mere non-dyadicity is insufficient for this
relative-distance condition. Then
$\|\varphi\|_{\mathrm{BMO}(\mathbb T)}\asymp\|\varphi\|_{\mathrm{BMO}_D(\mathbb T)}+\|\varphi(\cdot-2\delta\pi)\|_{\mathrm{BMO}_D(\mathbb T)}$
for all $\varphi\in\mathrm{BMO}(\mathbb T)$. Here classical BMO on the circle
uses all arcs, with arc length measure; it is distinct from the Euclidean
cube-based definition used by the page. Theorem 2.2 bounds the classical
seminorm by $4/d(\delta)$ times the maximum of the two dyadic seminorms;
the reverse bound follows because each dyadic arc is an arc.
Separately, on $\mathbb R$ one-grid dyadic BMO is strictly larger than
classical BMO: Kinnunen, Examples 3.5(3)-(4), records the witness
$f(x)=\log|x|$ for $x<0$ and $f(x)=-\log|x|$ for $x>0$, with $f(0)=0$.
Thus a single grid cannot replace arbitrary intervals on the line. Both
results are recorded here, not proved. The page works
with arbitrary cubes throughout and no item depends on this statement.

references.title: Tao Mei, BMO is the intersection of two translates of dyadic BMO, C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris 336 (2003), 1003-1006 (arXiv:math/0304417)
references.locator: Theorem 2.2 and its proof, printed p. 2; the relative-distance condition d(delta)>0 is defined on printed p. 1

references.title: Juha Kinnunen, Harmonic Analysis (Aalto University lecture notes)
references.locator: Examples 3.5(3)-(4), printed p. 39: the signed logarithm belongs to one-grid dyadic BMO on the line but not classical BMO

references.title: Brooke Wilson, Math 581A Classical and Multilinear Harmonic Analysis (University of Washington, Fall 2024), lecture 18
references.locator: the dyadic BMO definition and dyadic John-Nirenberg discussion, scanned pages 1-2

items.strategy: Record, without a Proof section, Mei Theorem 2.2 for circle arcs with 0<delta<1 and d(delta)>0. Separately record Kinnunen signed-logarithm strictness for one grid on the line. Keep proved_here false, the exact external-dependency record and source URLs, and do not promote the remark to a logical supplier.

external_dependency.exact_statement: For the unit circle T, with BMO(T) the classical BMO space and BMO_D(T) the dyadic BMO space of one fixed grid, there is a suitable non-dyadic shift delta such that ||phi||_{BMO(T)} is comparable to ||phi||_{BMO_D(T)} + ||phi(. - 2 delta pi)||_{BMO_D(T)} for all phi in BMO(T) (Mei, C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris 336 (2003), abstract and Introduction).
external_dependency.local_proof_attempt: None. The two-grid averaging/stopping argument of the cited paper is not reproduced; this page proves the classical cube-based duality directly and only records the distinction to prevent substituting a single dyadic grid's seminorm for the cube seminorm.
external_dependency.necessity: The page and several planned suppliers use dyadic stopping arguments in proofs; the remark prevents the invalid promotion of a single-grid dyadic seminorm to the adopted cube seminorm.

items.title: The logarithm is in BMO but not in L-infinity
items.statement:
Define $b:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ by $b(x)=\log|x|$ for $x\ne0$ and $b(0)=0$
(any finite value at the origin gives the same class). Then
$b\in\mathrm{BMO}(\mathbb R^n)$ with a seminorm depending only on $n$, and $b$
is unbounded on every neighbourhood of $0$; in particular no bounded
representative exists, so the continuous injection
$L^\infty/\mathbb C\to\mathrm{BMO}/\mathbb C$ of the A page is not surjective.

references.title: Mark Williams, Notes on Harmonic Analysis (January 11, 2022)
references.locator: Example 7.3 (log$|x|\in$BMO; reduce by $\log|rx|=\log|x|+\log r$), printed p. 30

references.title: Juha Kinnunen, Harmonic Analysis (Aalto University lecture notes)
references.locator: Examples 3.5(2), printed pp. 37-38

references.title: Terence Tao, Math 247A Lecture Notes 4 (UCLA, Fall 2006)
references.locator: Problem 3.2, printed p. 11

items.strategy: Dyadic shells prove local integrability. Scaling reduces mean oscillation to unit cubes; distant cubes use a gradient bound and nearby cubes a fixed logarithm integral. Every small punctured ball is a positive-measure superlevel, whereas essential-bound superlevels are null. Thus no bounded representative exists, including after adding a constant.

items.title: A BMO function need not be globally integrable
items.statement:
The claim refuted is the inclusion $\mathrm{BMO}(\mathbb R^n)\subseteq L^1(\mathbb R^n)$,
equivalently the claim that every BMO function is globally integrable. The
witness is the function $b(x)=\log|x|$ ($b(0)=0$) of
[[ex-logarithm-is-in-bmo-but-not-linfinity]], which satisfies
$\int_{\mathbb R^n}|b(x)|\,dx=+\infty$; hence
$\mathrm{BMO}(\mathbb R^n)\not\subseteq L^1(\mathbb R^n)$. Thus BMO membership alone does not guarantee a global Lebesgue pairing
$\int fb$: absolute integrability of the product $fb$ must be checked
separately. Such a pairing can exist even without cancellation of $f$.

references.title: Juha Kinnunen, Harmonic Analysis (Aalto University lecture notes)
references.locator: Examples 3.5(2) ($\log|x|\in$BMO with $|x|$-growth, hence no global integrability), printed pp. 37-38

references.title: Mark Williams, Notes on Harmonic Analysis (January 11, 2022)
references.locator: Example 7.3, printed p. 30

items.strategy: Restrict to the region $2<|x|<R$; in polar (or one-dimensional radial) coordinates the integral of $\log|x|$ over the annulus grows like $R^n\log R$, so it diverges as $R\to\infty$ for every $n\ge1$.

items.title: Integrating the John-Nirenberg tail recovers the Lq oscillation bound
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]).

Let $b\in\mathrm{BMO}(\mathbb R^n)$, $1\le q<\infty$ and let $Q$ be a cube.
Using the layer-cake formula and the John-Nirenberg exponential bound,
$|Q|^{-1}\int_Q|b-b_Q|^q=q\int_0^\infty\lambda^{q-1}|Q|^{-1}|\{x\in Q:|b(x)-b_Q|>\lambda\}|\,d\lambda\le C_{n,q}\|b\|_{\mathrm{BMO}}^q$,
with the zero-seminorm case giving $0$; this is the mechanism behind the
equivalence of the $L^q$ oscillation seminorms.

references.title: Mark Williams, Notes on Harmonic Analysis (January 11, 2022)
references.locator: (7.10) (the layer-cake computation from the exponential bound), printed p. 32

references.title: Juha Kinnunen, Harmonic Analysis (Aalto University lecture notes)
references.locator: Theorem 3.28 proof, printed pp. 53-54

items.strategy: Assume inherited Countable Choice. Insert John-Nirenberg into layer cake and scale lambda=mu*BMO; the finite gamma-type integral gives the q-th power bound for every 1<=q<infinity. Handle zero seminorm separately without division. Taking roots/suprema supplies the per-cube mechanism for oscillation equivalence.

items.title: Finite lacunary exponential sums belong to BMO
items.statement:
Let $0<a\le b<\infty$, and let $(\xi_n)_{n\in\mathbb Z}$ be nonzero real
frequencies satisfying
$a2^n\le|\xi_n|\le b2^n$ for every $n$. Let $(c_n)_{n\in\mathbb Z}$ have
finite support and put
$$f(x):=\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z}c_ne^{2\pi i\xi_nx}.$$
Then
$$\|f\|_{\mathrm{BMO}(\mathbb R)}\le C_{a,b,\phi}\Bigl(\sum_n|c_n|^2\Bigr)^{1/2}.$$
More precisely, fix a nonnegative $\phi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R)$ with
$\phi\ge1$ on $[-\tfrac12,\tfrac12]$. For an interval $I$ of length $L$ and
centre $x_I$, set $\phi_I(x):=\phi((x-x_I)/L)$. There is a constant
$c_I\in\mathbb C$ such that
$$\int_{\mathbb R}\phi_I(x)|f(x)-c_I|^2\,dx \le C_{a,b,\phi}L\sum_n|c_n|^2.$$

references.title: Terence Tao, Math 247A Lecture Notes 4 (UCLA, Fall 2006)
references.locator: Exercise Q4 (Lacunary exponential sums lie in BMO), printed pp. 26-27

items.strategy: Split at the least integer n0 with 2^n0 >= |I|^{-1}. For n<n0 choose the value of the low-frequency sum at the centre of I; its weighted L2 oscillation is bounded by the geometric sum of |xi_n|^2. For n>=n0, expand the weighted square and use integration by parts in the fixed smooth bump to obtain rapid decay in L|xi_n-xi_m|. Frequency comparability gives uniformly bounded absolute row sums: finitely many nearby indices are harmless, higher indices form a geometric tail, and lower indices are bounded by r(1+c 2^r)^(-M). The Schur estimate gives the high-frequency L2 bound. The bump dominates I, so Cauchy-Schwarz and the optimal-constant BMO inequality give the claimed seminorm bound. Finite sums only; no choice principle is used.
